candidates.draft_title: Add policy-gated download for member-owned session notes
candidates.snippet:
[EXTERNAL] Declan: Okay. So this comes directly from my members, repeatedly, and it's been building for months. People want to be able to download their own session notes.
[EXTERNAL] Declan: Right. So the way it works now — the member and coach have sessions, notes get taken, there's a reflection, action items, all that. And members can see them in the platform. But they can't take them with them. They can't export or download their own notes.
[EXTERNAL] Declan: They want a copy, and the reasons are actually good ones. First, some of them want to bring their dog's training notes to their own vet or a new trainer. Like, "here's the behavior we've been working on with the coach, here's the progress." They want to reference their dog's whole training journey in their own words.
[EXTERNAL] Declan: Second — and this one's more emotional — a few people have said they want their notes because the coaching has genuinely mattered to them and they want to keep it. Like a journal. If they ever left the company and lost platform access, all that reflection just... vanishes. And that feels wrong to them. It's their growth, their words.
[EXTERNAL] Declan: Exactly. It's theirs. They wrote it, or it's about them. And the ask is simple: let a member download their own session notes. A PDF, a text file, I don't care about the format. Just "here's your coaching history, it's yours to keep."
[EXTERNAL] Declan: That's an important distinction and yes. I'm not asking for a free-for-all. I'd want it to be something an org can allow or not. For us, we'd allow it — our whole philosophy is transparency, the notes belong to the person. But I can imagine a more locked-down company wanting to keep everything in the walls. So make it policy-gated. Where the org permits it, members can download their own notes.
[EXTERNAL] Declan: Yes. That's the ask, cleanly stated.
[EXTERNAL] Declan: It's more than nice. I've had at least a dozen people ask me directly, and a couple were genuinely disappointed — like it slightly soured the experience for them that they couldn't keep their own work. When your best engineers are the ones asking, and they're the retention risk, I take it seriously. It's not a dealbreaker, but it's a "you almost got this perfectly right and stopped one step short" kind of gap.
[EXTERNAL] Declan: You put it better than I did. Steal my thunder, please.
[EXTERNAL] Declan: Good. As long as it's captured properly I'm happy. I know these things take time. I just want it in the queue with a real rationale, not as a throwaway.

candidates.draft_title: Add post-project recovery training module for exhausted engineers
candidates.snippet:
[EXTERNAL] Declan: One more, purely logistical — when the signaling project wraps in the autumn, I'll have a cohort of exhausted engineers coming off eighteen months of hell. Can we do something for them specifically? A reset, almost.
[EXTERNAL] Declan: Exactly. I don't want them to burn out at the finish line, which is when it usually happens. You survive the marathon and collapse a step past the tape.
